problem.label: The gap
problem.title: Knowing AI matters isn’t the same as knowing what to do with it.
problem.lead: Most businesses aren’t short on interest. They’re short on answers to practical questions:
questions: Where are the real opportunities in our business, not the ones in the demos?
Which processes are actually worth improving?
Are the tools we already pay for good enough?
Where is automation justified, and where is it overkill?
What should stay in human hands?
How would we know if it worked?
problem.close: A product won’t answer those. Looking closely at how the work gets done will.

approach.label: What we do
approach.title: We start with the work, not the technology.
approach.lead: Five steps, in this order. Skip the first two, and you risk automating the wrong problem.

steps.title: Find the friction
steps.text: Understand where time, effort and information are being lost: the rework, the waiting, the double entry, the question someone answers ten times a day.

steps.title: Understand the process
steps.text: Map what actually happens, not what the procedure document says happens. That means talking to the people doing the work.

steps.title: Choose the right solution
steps.text: It might be AI, workflow automation, Microsoft 365 or Copilot features you already pay for, other existing software, a custom integration, or simply a better process. The problem decides, not the tool.

steps.title: Implement
steps.text: Integrate it into the actual business: your systems, your people, your way of working. Then adjust it once it meets the realities of day-to-day work.

steps.title: Measure
steps.text: Compare against where you started. If it didn’t create a meaningful improvement, you’ll hear that from us first.

examples.label: Where we help
examples.title: Friction worth looking at
examples.lead: The kinds of problems we investigate. None of them automatically calls for AI. Some need a better process, some need a tool you already have.
items: The same customer emails, answered by hand every day
Staff copying information from one system into another
Reports rebuilt manually every week or month
One task done three different ways by three different people
Critical knowledge that lives in one employee’s head
Microsoft 365 and Copilot licences nobody is really using
Systems that don’t talk to each other
Administrative work that eats hours but needs little judgment
Workflows held together by spreadsheets and email threads
Handoffs where work stalls because no one is sure who owns it next
examples.close: Recognize a few of these? That’s usually where the conversation starts.

principles.label: How we think
principles.title: The goal is better operations, not more AI.

items.title: Not every problem needs AI.
items.text: If a checklist, a clearer handoff or an inbox rule fixes it, that’s what we’ll recommend.

items.title: What you already own comes first.
items.text: Many businesses already pay for software that does what they need. We check before suggesting anything new.

items.title: Custom only when it’s justified.
items.text: We build custom workflows when existing tools genuinely don’t fit, not because building is more interesting.

items.title: Human-in-the-loop where it matters.
items.text: Human oversight stays where the consequences, ambiguity or judgment warrant it.

items.title: Not tied to any platform.
items.text: Microsoft, Google, existing SaaS, n8n or custom code: we choose what fits your business and your team.

principles.quote: Understand how the work actually happens first. Then decide whether technology should change it.
principles.origin: We come from hands-on operations work, where a process is only as good as how it holds up on a busy day.

about.label: About Ladea
about.title: An implementation partner, not a software vendor.
about.lead: Ladea Technologies is an AI implementation partner based in Montréal, Québec. Our work combines process improvement, workflow automation and AI integration, using the software a business already has wherever it genuinely fits.

items.text: Businesses that know AI matters but haven’t worked out what to implement, or that have tried tools that never quite stuck. Usually teams losing time to manual steps, re-keyed data and unclear handoffs.

In stages: an assessment first, then a defined implementation, a stabilization period, and ongoing support only where it’s justified. Each stage is scoped on its own. If you stop after the assessment, you keep the findings.
A software company. We have no platform to sell you, so recommendations follow the problem, not a product.
Based in Montréal. We work in English and French.

meta.description: How Ladea Technologies handles the information you send through the contact form on ladea.ca.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page explains what happens to the information you send us through the contact form on ladea.ca. It is short because the site collects very little.

sections.heading: Who we are
sections.body: Ladea Technologies is based in Montréal, Québec. For any question about your personal information, write to info@ladea.ca. That address also reaches the person responsible for the protection of personal information at Ladea Technologies.

sections.heading: What the contact form collects
sections.body:
• your name
  • your company name
  • your email address
  • your phone number, only if you choose to give it
  • your message

The form also records which language version of the site you used, so we can reply in the same language.

sections.heading: Why we collect it
sections.body: We use this information to respond to your inquiry and, if you want to continue the conversation, to follow up with you about it. We don’t use it for anything else.

sections.heading: No marketing lists
sections.body: We do not add you to a newsletter or marketing list. If we ever offer one, you will only be added if you explicitly opt in.

sections.heading: Who has access
sections.body: We don’t sell or rent your information. Your message reaches us through the tools we use to receive and manage inquiries, such as form-processing and email services. Those providers handle it on our behalf, and some of them may store data outside Québec.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.body: We keep inquiries only as long as we need them to respond and to follow up with you. You can ask us to delete your information at any time.

sections.heading: Your choices
sections.body: You can ask to see the personal information we hold about you, to correct it, or to have it deleted. Write to info@ladea.ca.

sections.heading: Cookies and tracking
sections.body: This site does not use cookies, analytics or advertising trackers, and it does not load third-party scripts or fonts. As with any website, our hosting provider may process technical data, such as IP addresses, to deliver and protect the site.

sections.heading: Changes to this page
sections.body: If our practices change, we will update this page and the date at the top.
